pairs.translation: First. Here is the text entitled Coemergent Joining. [N-A001](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a001)
I prostrate to the precious teachers. [N-A002](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a002)

Though never stirring from the basic space of intrinsic nature,
to act for the benefit of beings through compassionate responsiveness,
you came as an emanation embodiment, like a rainbow.
To Varahi of Uddiyana I prostrate. [N-A003](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a003)

Blessed in person by Varahi,
you attained accomplishment after cultivating for one session,
and brought the dakinis under your power.
To Lavapa I prostrate and offer praise. [N-A004](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a004)

Fearing that I myself might forget,
and to benefit a few fortunate people,
following the lord's spoken words,
I shall write the pith instructions on coemergent joining. [N-A001](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a001) [N-A006](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a006) [N-A007](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a007)

Concerning these pith instructions on coemergent joining,
the lord spoke these words:
“All the learned, the disciplined, and teachers of cultivation
say that this very Dharma is profound.” [N-A001](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a001) [N-A007](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a007) [N-A008](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a008) [N-A038](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a038)

Differentiating conceptualization and afflictions—
because it disciplines them all, it is Discipline. [N-A009](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a009) [N-A010](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a010)

That differentiating conceptualization is Dharma embodiment—
it is the basis for arousing certain knowing of this;
and because it cuts superimposition within,
these are pith instructions on valid cognition. [N-A007](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a007) [N-A010](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a010) [N-A011](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a011)

Eternalism, annihilationism, superimposition, and denigration:
free from such extremes, it is the Middle Way. [N-A010](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a010) [N-A012](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a012)

Since it cannot be spoken, thought, or expressed,
these are pith instructions on perfection. [N-A007](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a007) [N-A010](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a010)

The phenomena of samsara and nirvana
are complete within ordinary mind: thus it is the Great Perfection. [N-A010](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a010) [N-A013](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a013)

Good conceptualizing and bad conceptualizing, all of it—
not engaging the mental faculty with it is Mahamudra. [N-A014](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a014)
Because it pacifies suffering, it is Pacification. [N-A010](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a010)

All afflictions and differentiating conceptualization—
because it raises them onto the path, it is Secret Mantra. [N-A009](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a009) [N-A010](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a010)

Ordinary mind, differentiating conceptualization, and Dharma embodiment:
these three are coemergent from the beginning;
because the pith instruction joins them in ordinary mind,
it is explained as “coemergent joining.” [N-A001](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a001) [N-A007](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a007)

As for spirits, maras, and the like,
he said, it is also mantra against their obstacles. [N-A015](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a015)

Its meanings are summarized in six:
the teacher and the student,
putting on armor, the three kinds of discerning knowing,
experience, and benefits and results:
it is explained through these six meanings. [N-A002](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a002) [N-A016](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a016)

First, the qualifications of the student:
the venerable one spoke of two aspects,
those to reject and those to accept. [N-A017](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a017) [N-A038](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a038)

First, clinging at the time of the cause:
these manifold appearances of all that appears and exists,
like wealth and food in dreams,
are empty in their very appearance.
Failing to know that they are empty,
one takes food, wealth, and possessions,
sons, daughters, and wives,
through attachment to desirable objects,
to be permanent and real,
clinging to things as real. [N-A020](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a020)

One does not remember the Dharma for the next life,
and becomes intoxicated by the poison of desire.
Bound tightly by attachment and aversion,
one wanders in the three realms of samsara.
This is clinging at the time of the cause:
it is the first [type] to reject. [N-A013](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a013) [N-A021](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a021) [N-A038](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a038)

A certain individual, the supporting basis,
relies on a teacher versed in terminology
for years and months.
All the pith instructions on cultivation
are disparaged as having many ways to go astray.
Only the qualities of learning are discussed;
with phrases, terminology, and words,
only what is marked by characteristics is taught.
If this becomes nothing but learning, [N-A007](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a007) [N-A022](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a022)

the afflictions are not brought under control;
only the eight worldly concerns are pursued,
and one wanders in samsara for a long time.
Being taken in by a misguided spiritual friend:
this is held to be the second [type] to reject. [N-A009](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a009) [N-A013](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a013) [N-A019](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a019) [N-A023](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a023) [N-A038](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a038)

When it comes to knowing differentiating conceptualization as Dharma embodiment,
to reject differentiating conceptualization
and cultivate non-conceptual primordial knowing
is to seek Dharma embodiment elsewhere.
This is delusion in the condition of the object of focus,
said to be the third [type] to reject. [N-A018](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a018) [N-A024](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a024) [N-A038](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a038)

A certain excellent person,
with view, activity, and cultivation—
through the blessing of putting these into practice—
hopes to attain buddhahood;
if buddhahood is not attained,
fears falling into hell.
At the time of the immediate condition,
one falls into the two: hope and fear.
With the mental faculty thus divided,
this is considered the fourth [type] to reject. [N-A018](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a018) [N-A024](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a024) [N-A025](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a025) [N-A026](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a026) [N-A038](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a038)

First, a certain individual
understands attendants, material things, and possessions,
sons, daughters, and wives—
in brief, everything seen and heard without exception—
to be like an illusion.
Regarding all that appears as things,
neither taking them as real nor clinging apprehension arises.
Disenchanted with the phenomena of samsara,
one seeks pith instructions with faith and devotion.
This one, [not clinging] at the time of the cause,
is the first student to be accepted. [N-A007](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a007) [N-A013](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a013) [N-A028](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a028) [N-A038](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a038)

A person endowed with [faith and devotion]
goes to an excellent person,
is taught pith instructions on Dharma embodiment free of characteristics,
and understands that phenomena are without concrete existence.
At the time of the dominant condition,
this is being taken in hand by a spiritual friend:
this is the second qualified [student]. [N-A007](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a007) [N-A018](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a018) [N-A019](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a019) [N-A029](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a029) [N-A038](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a038)

A certain excellent person
has thoroughly received the teacher's pith instructions,
recognizes conceptual thought as ordinary mind,
and does not reject differentiating conceptualization;
one knows it to be Dharma embodiment itself.
Understanding conceptual thought's great kindness,
one carries conceptual thought onto the path:
there is no delusion at the time of the condition of the object of focus.
This is the third qualified student. [N-A002](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a002) [N-A007](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a007) [N-A018](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a018) [N-A024](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a024) [N-A030](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a030)

As differentiating conceptualization dissolves into Dharma embodiment,
one has no hope for buddhahood as good,
and no fear of samsara as bad.
Knowing them in their evenness,
at the time of the immediate condition,
one is free from the two: hope and fear.
This is the fourth qualification for acceptance. [N-A013](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a013) [N-A018](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a018) [N-A025](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a025) [N-A031](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a031) [N-A038](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a038)
Thus the qualifications of the student have been shown.

A student with those qualifications
must rely on a good teacher.
Second, the qualifications of the teacher:
there are four aspects of teachers as well:
a person who is a spiritual friend,
the teachings, appearance, and awareness. [N-A002](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a002) [N-A019](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a019) [N-A032](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a032) [N-A039](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a039)

First, the personal spiritual friend:
able to bring clarity, able to transform adverse circumstances,
undeluded, and able to open up discerning knowing—
these qualifications are stated in four aspects. [N-A002](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a002) [N-A019](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a019) [N-A033](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a033) [N-A034](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a034) [N-A038](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a038)

Whatever bad conceptualizing arises in an individual,
one transforms it into an aid to cultivation
and can restore the student's experiential acquaintance:
this is the teacher “able to offer supplication.” [N-A002](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a002) [N-A033](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a033) [N-A038](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a038)

The five deeds with immediate consequences and the ten nonvirtues,
broken vows and samaya, and the like,
are at odds with one's spiritual family and continuum.
Though such adverse circumstances of many kinds arise,
without [giving way to] intolerance for even an instant,
one knows these to be conceptual thought;
recognizing conceptual thought as ordinary mind,
one can transform ordinary mind itself into the four embodiments.
This is the teacher able to transform adverse circumstances. [N-A002](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a002) [N-A034](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a034) [N-A035](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a035) [N-A038](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a038)

When differentiating conceptualization arises,
one knows it as one's own teacher with vivid clarity,
and understands conceptual thought to be kind.
Dharma embodiment and differentiating conceptualization
are not in the least different:
when this firm, certain knowing arises,
that is my undeluded teacher. [N-A002](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a002) [N-A024](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a024) [N-A030](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a030) [N-A034](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a034) [N-A036](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a036) [N-A038](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a038)

Differentiating conceptualization is known as ordinary mind,
and ordinary mind itself is known as non-arising.
There is no differentiating conceptualization to reject,
and no non-conceptual primordial knowing to accomplish.
These diverse appearances of conceptual thought,
like salt added to water,
are nondual with emptiness.
The teacher who shows this
is the teacher who opens up discerning knowing. [N-A002](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a002) [N-A024](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a024) [N-A034](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a034) [N-A037](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a037) [N-A038](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a038)

Thus, for the personal spiritual friend,
four aspects of qualifications have been explained. [N-A019](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a019) [N-A038](../translations/NOTES.md#n-a038)

notes.problem: The whole title is absent from the glossary. Line1 has ལྷན་གཅིག་; later instances have ལྷན་ཅིག་, and lines20–21 abbreviate the expression as སྐྱེས་སྦྱོར་. Lines42–45 explicitly relate three items and explain the name.
notes.treatment: Use coemergent joining provisionally, coemergent for ལྷན་ཅིག་སྐྱེས་, and retain ordinary mind, differentiating conceptualization, and Dharma embodiment as distinct labels. In line44 them resumes these three; in ordinary mind renders སེམས་སུ་. The ordinal First in line1 is retained.
notes.uncertainty: The naming relation is locally supported; the exact philosophical force of joining remains open. The glossary has co-emergent ignorance but no standalone joining entry; the compound spelling is not a general approval.
notes.review_action: Review the title and coemergent-joining family proposals; check the precise syntactic force of སེམས་སུ་སྦྱོར་ against a reliable witness.

notes.problem: Standalone བླ་མ་ is absent; the existing Guru Yoga whole-expression entry does not establish a universal English mapping.
notes.treatment: Use teacher provisionally in this work; preserve master-disciple relations through explicit syntax and lineage references.
notes.uncertainty: Scoped working mapping only, not owner-approved terminology.
notes.review_action: Review the teacher proposal; retain existing Guru Yoga wherever that complete expression occurs.

notes.problem: In འགྲོ་བའི་དོན་མཛད་, literal meaning (the standalone glossary output for དོན་) would misconstrue the beneficiary construction. སྤྲུལ་སྐུ་ abbreviates the glossary expression སྤྲུལ་པའི་སྐུ་. Varahi of Uddiyana is the named addressee.
notes.treatment: Use benefit for this construction only; retain compassionate responsiveness, basic space, intrinsic nature, and emanation embodiment. Varahi is a transliterated name without adding Vajra.
notes.uncertainty: The beneficiary construction is clear; historical identification beyond the supplied name is not established.
notes.review_action: Review the scoped དོན་ usage and name transliterations; do not extend benefit to the six meanings at48–52.

notes.problem: Line7 reads དོངས་སུ་ rather than expected དངོས་སུ་. Accomplishment and dakini are technical gaps; the Sanskrit form of the name ལྭ་བ་པ་ is not independently verified.
notes.treatment: Blessed in person provisionally interprets the defective sequence as དངོས་སུ་; no source change. Lavapa is a conservative Roman spelling. Accomplishment renders དངོས་གྲུབ་ and dakinis renders མཁའ་འགྲོ་ provisionally. The subject of all three preceding lines is Lavapa.
notes.uncertainty: Likely typographic defect; identification with a specific historically attested Lavapa remains unverified.
notes.review_action: Check line7 and the name against a witness; review technical additions.

notes.tibetan:
དེ་ཡི་བྱིན་རླབས་རཀྵི་ཏ། །
དེེ་ཡི་བརྒྱུད་འཛིན་ལྷོ་བྲག་པ། །
དེ་ཡིི་བྱིན་རླབས་གུང་ཐང་པ། །
མི་ལའི་ཐུགས་ཀྱི་སྲས་གྱུར་པ། །
རྗེ་མཚན་ལྡན་བླ་མ་རིན་པོ་ཆེ། །
བརྒྱུད་པའི་བླ་མ་རྣམས་ལ་བདག་ཕྱག་འཚལ། །
notes.problem: The lineage verse is elliptical: “his blessing, Rakshita”; “his blessing, Gungthangpa.” The referents of successive དེ་ are implicit. The standalone ཐུགས་ has no glossary entry, and ཐུགས་ཀྱི་སྲས་ is an honorific lineage expression.
notes.treatment: Bracket recipient of where the draft supplies the relation. Preserve Rakshita, Lhodrakpa, Gungthangpa, and Mila without expanding them into historical identities. Render son of the heart as a scoped whole expression, not an approved standalone ཐུགས་ equivalent. The fully qualified lord/teacher is the disciple described in line14.
notes.uncertainty: Beneficiary reading of blessing is likely but elliptical; historical identifications and the precise lineage succession require verification.
notes.review_action: Check the lineage against a reliable edition; approve or revise the whole-expression heart-son proposal.

notes.problem: Line19 has ལྟ་རྗེའི་, an irregular teacher-attribution phrase; the rough reference reads masters of the view. Line17 says the writer fears forgetting, not that a great person is forgotten.
notes.treatment: Following the lord’s spoken words treats ལྟ་ as an unresolved extraneous syllable; its source presence is preserved here and in Tibetan. Render the writer’s stated purpose and future intention, not a completed composition.
notes.uncertainty: The intended word before རྗེའི་ is unverified; lord is provisional at this locus.
notes.review_action: Check line19 against a witness and confirm whether ལྟ་ carries content that should replace the current treatment.

notes.problem: གདམས་ངག་ and the instruction verb/form གདམས་ are absent from the glossary.
notes.treatment: Use pith instructions, with singular pith instruction for the instrumental naming explanation in line44.
notes.uncertainty: Provisional local mapping only.
notes.review_action: Review the pith-instruction entry and its linked grammatical realization.

notes.problem: མཁས་བཙུན་སྒོམ་སྟོན་ may enumerate the learned, the disciplined, and cultivation teachers, or qualify one group of teachers. The speech opening at22 has no typographic closing quote.
notes.treatment: Read three coordinated groups. Quote the immediate report at23–24; the subsequent doctrinal explanations remain attributable to the reported teaching without invented speech punctuation boundaries.
notes.uncertainty: Alternative single-group reading remains plausible.
notes.review_action: Confirm coordination and quotation extent with a reliable edition.

notes.problem: ཉོན་མོངས་པ་ and its abbreviated forms lack a standalone glossary row.
notes.treatment: Use afflictions consistently and provisionally; do not substitute generic emotions or merge them with differentiating conceptualization.
notes.uncertainty: No owner approval recorded for the new term.
notes.review_action: Review the afflictions proposal.

སྡུག་བསྔལ་ཞི་བས་ཞི་བྱེད་ཡིན། །
ལམ་དུ་སློངས་པས་གསང་སྔགས་ཡིན། །
notes.problem: The parallel passage names Discipline, valid cognition, the Middle Way, perfection, Great Perfection, Pacification, and Secret Mantra. Most labels are absent from the glossary; the perfection line lacks ཤེས་རབ་.
notes.treatment: Preserve each classification and its stated causal explanation. Perfection does not add discerning knowing, which occurs only in the longer glossary expression. Discipline and Pacification retain the wordplay with disciplines and pacifies.
notes.uncertainty: Named-tradition interpretations are contextual; the source itself gives no expanded titles or doctrinal citations.
notes.review_action: Review the local term proposals without importing additional systems or claims.

notes.problem: Line28 ends བསྐྱེད་པའི་ས།, literally a basis/place for arousing; an expected causal ending would give a different construction.
notes.treatment: Translate the supplied noun ས་ as basis and supply it is to connect the clauses. Certain knowing concerns differentiating conceptualization as Dharma embodiment. No causal-ending emendation is made.
notes.uncertainty: The noun construction may itself be a transcription error.
notes.review_action: Check the ending of line28; revise the English construction only with disclosed evidence.

notes.problem: རྟག་ཆད་སྒྲོ་སྐུར་ is a compact paired enumeration; only the superimposition family is established.
notes.treatment: Expand grammatically to eternalism, annihilationism, superimposition, and denigration; preserve the two linked pairs and the freedom-from-extremes relation.
notes.uncertainty: Provisional technical expansions; no claim that this is an exhaustive definition of the Middle Way.
notes.review_action: Review the proposed abbreviated-form terminology.

notes.problem: Standalone འཁོར་བ་ and མྱ་ངན་འདས་པ་ are not glossary entries. Their abbreviation at35 is resolved from the explicit pairing.
notes.treatment: Use samsara and nirvana provisionally; preserve ordinary mind as the location in which their phenomena are complete.
notes.uncertainty: No translation of the source into a claim that samsara and nirvana are surpassed is warranted here.
notes.review_action: Review the samsara and nirvana proposals.

notes.problem: ཡིད་ལ་མི་བྱེད་ is an attention/engagement construction. Rendering it as mere absence of ordinary mind would erase the separate mental-faculty assignment. ཕྱག་རྒྱ་ཆེ་ is the metrical abbreviation of the established Mahamudra headword.
notes.treatment: Not engaging the mental faculty with it retains the mental-faculty component and the negation. Good and bad conceptualizing retains the form རྟོག་ rather than silently replacing it by the separate conceptual-thought entry.
notes.uncertainty: Precise English syntax of non-engagement remains a proposed construction.
